def run(_context):
    import adsk.core, adsk.fusion, adsk.cam
    app = adsk.core.Application.get()
    doc = app.activeDocument
    print("doc:", doc.name)
    des = adsk.fusion.Design.cast(app.activeProduct)
    products = doc.products
    for i in range(products.count):
        print("product:", products.item(i).productType)
    cam = adsk.cam.CAM.cast(products.itemByProductType("CAMProductType"))
    if cam:
        print("setups:", cam.setups.count)
        for s in cam.setups:
            print("  setup:", s.name, s.operationType, "ops:", s.operations.count, "bodies:", s.models.count)
    return None

  "message": "=== inspect ()
Compact scene summary: units, bodies (dims/bbox in mm), CAM setups.

One call replaces a pile of exploration scripts. Returns a JSON-able dict.
=== add_operation (setup, *, strategy, tool, geometry=None, body_index=0, name=None)
Add an operation to a setup. Required decisions:
  strategy: Fusion strategy string ("face","pocket2d","adaptive2d","contour2d",...)
  tool:     document-tool index (int) or description substring
  geometry: {"faces":[idx,...], "type":"pocket"|"contour"|"drill", "loop":.., "side":..}
            REQUIRED for area/contour/drilling strategies; omit for "face".
            For drilling-family strategies (drill, center drill, spot drill,
            bore, counterbore, tap) pass type="drill" with the hole faces.

Tool is attached on the INPUT before add() (post-add setter is unreliable).
Returns {"operation": <name>, "params": {param_name: {value, expression}, ...}}
— the full Fusion parameter list is included so you can read param names and
units, then pass them all to mb.set_params() in one call.
=== add_tool (library_url, index=None)
Add the chosen library tool to the document tool library; return its
document-tool index + summary. Re-fetches the library by URL (stable across
scripts) and the tool by index. Also accepts the whole dict row that
list_library_tools() returned (url + index pulled from it).
=== make_tool (json_str)
Synthesize a tool from a Fusion tool JSON (geometry in mm; model-supplied),
add it to the document tool library, return its document-tool index.
=== set_geometry (op_name, geometry, body_index=0)
Set or replace the geometry selection on an existing operation.
Use this to fix a geometry error from add_operation() without recreating the op.
geometry: {"faces":[idx,...], "type":"pocket"|"contour", "loop":.., "side":..}
=== list_library_tools (contains=None, location='local', limit=200)
Available tools across local tool libraries (the model CHOOSES one).

Returns [{library_url, index, description, diameter_mm, corner_radius_mm,
flute_length_mm, flutes}]. `contains` filters by case-insensitive substring of
the library URL or tool description (e.g. "TIW"). Pass a returned
(library_url, index) to add_tool().
=== probe ()
Compact CAM state: setups + ops with tool/step params (mm). For verifying
your work before you finish. A finished, VALID op can still carry
has_warning=True (e.g. regions skipped as unreachable under current ramping
constraints) — included here, at the end-of-run verify step ONLY, so
transient mid-build warnings never spam the working loop; inspect such ops
in the UI or reconsider their parameters if coverage matters.
=== strategy_guide (strategy: str) -> dict
Parameter map for a strategy captured without geometry attached.

Returns {param_name: {"expression": <default_expr>, "unit": <set_params_unit>}}.
Covers most params (stepover, stepdown, feeds, speeds, heights, passes,
compensation). A small number of geometry-dependent params may be absent —
the "params" dict returned by add_operation() is the definitive list for
a specific op once geometry is set.

Use this before set_params() to look up exact parameter names without
guessing. "unit" is the unit= string for set_params():
  "mm"     → length in mm or feed in mm/min
  "raw"    → dimensionless (RPM, counts, ratios, angles)
  "bool"   → True/False flag (e.g. doMultipleDepths)
  "choice" → quoted string for mode params (e.g. bottomHeight_mode)

Returns {} for unknown/unprobed strategies.
=== generate (setup=None, operation=None, timeout=120)
Generate toolpaths and WAIT. Pass a setup name (all its ops) or an op name.
Returns per-op {name, has_toolpath, is_valid}.
=== post (setup, *, output_path, units='mm', post_file=None, number=1001)
Post-process a setup to NC. units: "mm"|"in". post_file defaults to a
generic mill .cps. Returns {"nc_path": output_path}.
=== set_params (op_name, params)
Set multiple parameters on an operation in one call.
  params: {param_name: {"value": <v>, "unit": "mm"|"raw"|"bool"|"choice"}, ...}
Use the param names and expressions returned by add_operation() or list_params()
to build this dict. Wrong param name → error listing all available names.
Returns {param_name: {value, unit}, ...} for every param that was set."
}
